options.summary: Human-gated agentic tree search: narrow, experimentally defensible core contribution focused on where human branch and claim gates change an AI Scientist-v2 trajectory.
evidence: High human_leverage score 5 and lower risk score 2
risks: Requires matched autonomous versus human-gated comparisons before claiming superiority.

options.summary: AI Co-Scientist-style debate front-end before AI Scientist-v2 experiment generation.
risks: Benefit may disappear once hypotheses are constrained by runnable benchmarks.

options.summary: AlphaEvolve-style subproblem optimization inside automated research, implemented with OpenEvolve because official AlphaEvolve core code is unavailable.
risks: Local program improvements may not improve paper-level scientific quality.

options.summary: Full end-to-end co-pilot architecture combining hypothesis debate, AI Scientist-v2 automation, human gates, and OpenEvolve program search.
risks: Highest scope risk; needs staging to avoid a broad but weak paper.

human_decision: Select hitl-gated-tree-search as the narrow core paper, while retaining co-scientist and OpenEvolve modules as supporting layers.
rationale: The selected direction has the best balance of novelty, testability, paper value, human leverage, and risk. It lets the paper make a defensible systems contribution now while treating the full co-pilot v3 architecture as the broader target.
follow_up_checks: Run matched autonomous versus human-gated branch continuations before claiming outcome improvement.
Keep full-system superiority as a target claim until multi-task evidence exists.
Record every later human gate with the shared JSON schema.
